entry.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving. Agentic services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs.
entry.summary:
Agentic services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs. In this scenario, existing systems (1) overlook tool-return readiness in service evaluation, wasting limited resources, and (2) use heuristic strategies to decide admission and placement on GPUs, resulting in suboptimal scheduling decisions. To bridge this gap, we present TAO, a tool-aware joint scheduling framework for LLM-based agentic serving.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #agents

entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution
entry.summary:
Agentic Entity Resolution (ER) systems iteratively plan actions, retrieve evidence, revise hypotheses, and propose graph mutations. An erroneous identity hypothesis may condition later retrieval and produce apparent confirmation. This paper proposes a Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI)-informed authorization boundary between evidence available for agent reasoning and evidence eligible to authorize persistent identity-changing mutations.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #ml-theory #cryptography

entry.title: Analyzing Compiler-induced Constant-time Violations with Compiler at Scale. The constant-time programming policy is a de facto standard for cryptographic libraries to prevent timing side-channel attacks.
entry.summary:
The constant-time programming policy is a de facto standard for cryptographic libraries to prevent timing side-channel attacks. However, compiler optimizations may break constant-time source code during compilation. Systematically preventing this requires understanding where a violation arises, how it is introduced, and which compiler configurations are problematic.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #compilers #combinatorics
